event-title.$: ENTRY INTO FORCE OF REQUEST FOR SUBSTANTIVE EXAMINATION

section.content: 本发明提供一种能够在车辆中高效地进行神经网络模型的学习的机器学习装置。设于车辆的机器学习装置具备：学习计划部(81)，其制作神经网络模型的学习计划；数据集制作部(82)，其取得多个输入参数的实测值和至少一个输出参数的实测值来制作训练数据集；学习部(83)，其在车辆停着时进行神经网络模型的学习；以及停车期间预测部(84)，其预测车辆的停车期间。数据集制作部将训练数据集分到基于多个输入参数的各个范围确定的多个学习区域。学习部按各学习区域进行神经网络模型的学习。学习计划部将多个学习区域分配到停车期间以使得在停车期间中神经网络模型的学习不中断。

The invention provides a machine learning device capable of efficiently learning a neural network model in a vehicle. A machine learning device provided in a vehicle is provided with: a learning planning unit (81) for creating a learning plan of the neural network model; a data set creation unit (82) that creates a training data set by acquiring measured values of a plurality of input parameters and measured values of at least one output parameter; a learning unit (83) that learns a neural network model when the vehicle is stopped; and a parking period prediction unit (84) that predicts the parking period of the vehicle. The data set creating unit divides the training data set into a plurality of learning regions determined based on respective ranges of the plurality of input parameters. The learning unit learns the neural network model for each learning region. The learning planning section assigns a plurality of learning regions to the parking period so that learning of the neural network model is not interrupted during the parking period.

Machine learning deviceTechnical Field

The present invention relates to a machine learning device.

Background

Conventionally, it has been known to calculate predetermined output parameters from predetermined input parameters using a neural network model including an input layer, a hidden layer, and an output layer. For example, in the control device for an internal combustion engine described in patent document 1, the flow rate of intake gas to be taken into a combustion chamber of the internal combustion engine is estimated using a learned neural network model.

Documents of the prior art

Patent document 1: japanese patent laid-open publication No. 2012-112277

Disclosure of Invention

Technical problem to be solved by the invention

However, when the learned neural network model is applied to a vehicle, the characteristics of the vehicle may change due to aging or the like. In this case, the correspondence relationship between the input parameters and the output parameters changes, and the accuracy of calculating the output parameters by the neural network model decreases. Further, the characteristics of the vehicle are somewhat different for each vehicle.

Therefore, in order to improve the accuracy of calculating the output parameters, it is considered to acquire a training data set for learning in the vehicle and to learn the neural network model in the vehicle. However, a control device that can be used for learning needs to control a drive source (an internal combustion engine, a motor, or the like) of the vehicle during running of the vehicle. Therefore, it is difficult to perform learning with a high computational load during vehicle travel.

Then, it is considered that the neural network model is learned while the vehicle is stopped. However, if the learning time is longer than the parking period, the learning cannot be completed during the parking period. As a result, the neural network model may not be updated at an appropriate frequency, and the accuracy of calculating the output parameters based on the neural network model may deteriorate.

In view of the above problems, it is an object of the present invention to provide a machine learning device capable of efficiently learning a neural network model in a vehicle.

Means for solving the problems

The gist of the present disclosure is as follows.

(1) A machine learning device provided in a vehicle, comprising: a learning planning unit that creates a learning plan of a neural network model that outputs at least one output parameter from a plurality of input parameters; a data set creating unit that creates a training data set by acquiring measured values of the plurality of input parameters and measured values of the at least one output parameter corresponding to the measured values; a learning unit that performs learning of the neural network model using the training data set while the vehicle is stopped, based on the learning plan; and a parking period prediction unit that predicts a parking period of the vehicle, wherein the data set creation unit divides the training data set into a plurality of learning regions determined based on respective ranges of the plurality of input parameters, the learning unit performs learning of the neural network model for each learning region, and the learning planning unit assigns the plurality of learning regions to the parking period so that the learning of the neural network model is not interrupted during the parking period.

(2) The machine learning device according to (1) above, wherein the plurality of learning regions include a primary learning region and a university learning region including the primary learning region, the primary learning region and the university learning region are set such that a data density of the primary learning region is higher than a data density of the university learning region, and the learning planning unit selectively allocates the primary learning region and the university learning region to the parking period.

(3) According to the machine learning device described in the above (1), the plurality of learning regions are given learning priorities.

(4) According to the machine learning device described in the above (3), the learning planning unit increases a priority of learning in a learning region including a value of the input parameter having a relatively high frequency of occurrence, compared with a priority of learning in a learning region including a value of the input parameter having a relatively low frequency of occurrence.

(5) According to the machine learning device described in the above (3), the learning planning unit changes the priority order of learning based on information on a road on which the vehicle is traveling or a warm-up state of an internal combustion engine provided in the vehicle.

ADVANTAGEOUS EFFECTS OF INVENTION

According to the present invention, it is possible to provide a machine learning device capable of efficiently learning a neural network model in a vehicle.

Detailed Description

Hereinafter, embodiments of the present invention will be described in detail with reference to the drawings. In the following description, the same reference numerals are given to the same components.

< first embodiment >

First, a first embodiment of the present invention will be described with reference to fig. 1 to 10.

< description of the entirety of internal Combustion Engine >

Fig. 1 is a diagram schematically showing an internal combustion engine to which a machine learning device according to a first embodiment is applied. The internal combustion engine 1 is a spark ignition type internal combustion engine (for example, a gasoline engine) that ignites an air-fuel mixture with an ignition plug, and is provided in a vehicle.

The internal combustion engine 1 includes an engine body 3. The engine body 3 includes a cylinder block in which a plurality of cylinders 2 are formed, a cylinder head in which an intake port and an exhaust port are formed, and a crankcase. The cylinder head is provided with an intake valve configured to open and close an intake port, an exhaust valve configured to open and close an exhaust port, a fuel injection valve for directly injecting fuel into a combustion chamber, and an ignition plug for generating spark.

In the present embodiment, the number of cylinders 2 is four. An intake manifold 4 and an exhaust manifold 5 are connected to each cylinder 2.

The intake manifold 4 is connected to an outlet of a compressor 7a of a turbocharger 7 via an intake pipe 6. An inlet of the compressor 7a is connected to an air cleaner 8 via an intake pipe 6. A throttle valve 9 driven by a throttle valve drive actuator is disposed in the intake pipe 6. Further, an intercooler 13 for cooling the intake air flowing through the intake pipe 6 is disposed around the intake pipe 6. Further, the intercooler 13 may also be internally provided to the intake manifold 4. The intake manifold 4 and the intake pipe 6 form an intake passage that guides air into the cylinders 2.

On the other hand, the exhaust manifold 5 is connected to an inlet of a turbine 7b of the turbocharger 7 via an exhaust pipe 27. The outlet of the turbine 7b is connected to a catalyst 29 via an exhaust pipe 27. The catalyst 29 is, for example, a three-way catalyst that purifies HC, CO, NOx, and the like in the exhaust gas. The exhaust manifold 5 and the exhaust pipe 27 form an exhaust passage through which exhaust gas generated by combustion of the air-fuel mixture is discharged from the cylinders 2.

The exhaust passage and the intake passage are connected to each other via an exhaust gas recirculation passage (EGR passage, exhaust gas recirculation passage) 14. The EGR passage 14 recirculates a part of the exhaust gas flowing in the exhaust passage to the intake passage as EGR gas. Further, an electronically controlled EGR control valve 15 is provided in the EGR passage 14. The EGR control valve 15 adjusts the amount of EGR gas recirculated from the exhaust passage to the intake passage. Further, an EGR cooler 16 that cools the EGR gas is provided in the EGR passage 14.

In the present embodiment, the EGR passage 14 is connected to the exhaust passage on the downstream side of the catalyst 29 and the intake passage on the upstream side of the compressor 7a, and therefore, the internal combustion engine 1 is provided with the EGR system of the so-called low pressure circulation system (L P L system), and the internal combustion engine 1 may be provided with the EGR system of another system, for example, the internal combustion engine 1 may be provided with the EGR system of the so-called high pressure circulation system (HP L system), and in this case, the EGR passage is connected to the exhaust manifold 5 and the intake manifold 4, for example.

The configuration of the internal combustion engine 1 is not limited to the above configuration. Therefore, the specific configuration of the internal combustion engine, such as the cylinder arrangement, the fuel injection method, the configuration of the intake/exhaust system, the configuration of the valve operating mechanism, the configuration of the supercharger, and the presence or absence of the supercharger, may be different from the configuration shown in fig. 1. For example, the fuel injection valve may also be configured to inject fuel into the intake port.

< construction of ECU >

A vehicle equipped with the internal combustion engine 1 is provided with an Electronic Control Unit (ECU). Fig. 2 is a diagram schematically showing the configuration of the ECU. The ECU60 includes a communication interface 61, a memory 62, and a processor 63, and executes various controls of the vehicle. For example, various controls of the internal combustion engine 1 are executed by the ECU60 based on outputs of various sensors and the like. In the present embodiment, one ECU60 is provided, but a plurality of ECUs may be provided for each function.

The communication interface 61 has an interface circuit for connecting the ECU60 to an in-vehicle Network conforming to CAN (Controller Area Network) or other standards. The ECU60 communicates with other in-vehicle devices via the communication interface 61.

The memory 62 includes, for example, a volatile semiconductor memory (e.g., RAM) and a nonvolatile semiconductor memory (e.g., ROM). The memory 62 stores a program executed in the processor 63, various data used when various processes are executed by the processor 63, and the like.

The processor 63 has one or more CPUs (Central Processing units) and peripheral circuits thereof, and executes various processes. The processor 63 may also have an arithmetic circuit such as a logical operation unit or a numerical operation unit. The communication interface 61, the memory 62, and the processor 63 are connected to each other via signal lines.

The ECU60 is connected to the actuator 91 via an in-vehicle network, and controls the actuator 91. In the present embodiment, the actuator 91 includes a fuel injection valve, an ignition plug, a throttle valve driving actuator, the EGR control valve 15, and the like.

In addition, the vehicle is provided with a GPS receiver 92. The GPS receiver 92 receives signals from three or more GPS satellites and detects the current position of the vehicle (for example, the latitude and longitude of the vehicle). The GPS receiver 92 is connected to the ECU60 via an in-vehicle network, and an output of the GPS receiver 92 is transmitted to the ECU 60.

In addition, a map database 93 is provided in the vehicle. The map database 93 stores map information. The map information includes road information such as road position information, road shape information (for example, types of a curve and a straight line portion, a curvature radius of the curve, a road gradient, and the like), a road type, and a vehicle speed limit. The map database 93 is connected to the ECU60 via an in-vehicle network, and the ECU60 acquires map information from the map database 93.

In addition, a navigation system 94 is provided in the vehicle. The navigation system 94 sets a travel route of the vehicle to the destination based on the current position of the vehicle detected by the GPS receiver 92, map information of the map database 93, an input by the driver of the vehicle, and the like. The navigation system 94 is connected to the ECU60 via an in-vehicle network, and the travel route set by the navigation system 94 is transmitted to the ECU 60. The GPS receiver 92 and the map database 93 may be incorporated in the navigation system 94.

In addition, a communication module 95 is provided in the vehicle. The communication module 95 is a device that enables communication between the vehicle and the outside of the vehicle. The communication module 95 includes, for example, a data communication module (dcm), a short-range wireless communication module, and the like. The vehicle communicates with a server or the like outside the vehicle via the data communication module. The vehicle communicates with the road-side device by road-to-vehicle communication and communicates with the vehicle by vehicle-to-vehicle communication via the short-range wireless module. The information received by the communication module 95 is sent to the ECU 60.

The ECU60 receives the outputs of the air flow meter 71, the air-fuel ratio sensor 72, the NOx sensor 73, the crank angle sensor 74, the load sensor 75, the torque sensor 76, and the vehicle speed sensor 77.

The airflow meter 71 detects the flow rate of air in the intake passage. As shown in fig. 1, the air flow meter 71 is disposed in the intake pipe 6 between the air cleaner 8 and the compressor 7 a. The air flow meter 71 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and the output of the air flow meter 71 is sent to the ECU 60.

The air-fuel ratio sensor 72 detects the air-fuel ratio of the exhaust gas. As shown in fig. 1, the air-fuel ratio sensor 72 is disposed in the exhaust pipe 27 between the turbine 7b and the catalyst 29. The air-fuel ratio sensor 72 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and the output of the air-fuel ratio sensor 72 is sent to the ECU 60.

The NOx sensor 73 detects the concentration of nitrogen oxides (NOx) in the exhaust gas. As shown in fig. 1, the NOx sensor 73 is disposed in the exhaust pipe 27 between the turbine 7b and the catalyst 29. The NOx sensor 73 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and the output of the NOx sensor 73 is sent to the ECU 60.

The crank angle sensor 74 generates an output pulse every time the crankshaft of the internal combustion engine 1 rotates by a predetermined angle (for example, 10 degrees). The crank angle sensor 74 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and the output of the crank angle sensor 74 is sent to the ECU 60. The ECU60 calculates the engine speed based on the output of the crank angle sensor 74.

The load sensor 75 is connected to an accelerator pedal provided in the vehicle, and detects a depression amount of the accelerator pedal. The load sensor 75 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and the output of the load sensor 75 is sent to the ECU 60. The ECU60 calculates the engine load based on the output of the load sensor 75.

The torque sensor 76 is disposed on, for example, a crankshaft of the internal combustion engine 1, and detects the output torque of the internal combustion engine 1. The torque sensor 76 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and the output of the torque sensor 76 is sent to the ECU 60.

The vehicle speed sensor 77 is provided in the vehicle and detects the speed of the vehicle. The vehicle speed sensor 77 is electrically connected to the ECU60, and the output of the vehicle speed sensor 77 is sent to the ECU 60.

In the present embodiment, the ECU60 also functions as a machine learning device provided in the vehicle to learn the neural network model.

< learning of neural network model in vehicle >)

In the present embodiment, a neural network model as shown in fig. 3 is actually mounted on a vehicle (specifically, ECU 60). In the present embodiment, the target of the neural network model is the internal combustion engine 1. Therefore, the neural network model outputs at least one output parameter of the internal combustion engine 1 in accordance with a plurality of input parameters of the internal combustion engine 1.

The neural network model is learned (i.e., the weights w and the offsets b are set) before the vehicle is shipped from the factory. In the learning of the neural network model, a training data set including a combination of an actual measurement value of an input parameter and an actual measurement value of an output parameter corresponding to the actual measurement value of the input parameter is used. Specifically, the values of the weights w and the bias b in the neural network model are repeatedly updated by the error back propagation method described above using a large number of training data sets. As a result, the neural network model is learned, and the learned neural network model is created.

However, the actual internal combustion engine 1 provided in the vehicle on which the neural network model is actually mounted is not used for a large number of training data sets, but is acquired in advance by an internal combustion engine that is manufactured using training data, such as an engine mount. Further, the characteristics of the internal combustion engine 1 may be somewhat different from those of the internal combustion engine for training data preparation. Therefore, it is possible to cause the learned neural network model to not accurately conform to the characteristics of the internal combustion engine 1. In addition, the characteristics of the internal combustion engine 1 may change due to aging or the like.

Therefore, in the present embodiment, in order to improve the accuracy of the output parameters calculated by the neural network model, the neural network model is also learned in the vehicle using the ECU 60. Thus, the neural network model can accurately match the characteristics of the internal combustion engine 1, and the accuracy of the output parameters calculated by the neural network model is improved.

Fig. 4 is a functional block diagram of the ECU 60. In the present embodiment, the ECU60 includes a learning planning unit 81, a data set creation unit 82, a learning unit 83, a parking period prediction unit 84, a calculation unit 85, and a control unit 86. These are functional blocks that are realized by the processor 63 of the ECU60 executing programs stored in the memory 62 of the ECU 60.

The learning planning unit 81 creates a learning plan of a neural network model that outputs at least one output parameter from a plurality of input parameters. The data set creating unit 82 obtains measured values of a plurality of input parameters and measured values of output parameters corresponding to the measured values to create a training data set. The training data set includes a combination of measured values of a plurality of input parameters and measured values of output parameters corresponding to the measured values. The learning unit 83 learns the neural network model using the training data set acquired in the vehicle by the data set generating unit 82 based on the learning plan generated by the learning planning unit 81.

The neural network model is stored in the memory 62 of the ECU 60. The neural network model has, for example, the configuration shown in fig. 3. The number of layers of the neural network model may be any number of three or more layers. The number of nodes in the input layer may be any number of two or more. The number of nodes in each hidden layer and output layer may be one or more.

The parking period prediction unit 84 predicts a parking period of the vehicle (hereinafter, simply referred to as "parking period"). Specifically, the parking period prediction unit 84 predicts the date and time (parking date and time) when the parking period is generated and the time length (parking time) of the parking period. The stop of the vehicle means a state where the vehicle speed is zero. Therefore, the parking of the vehicle includes a state in which the vehicle is temporarily stopped before a traffic light, a state in which the vehicle is temporarily stopped due to a traffic jam, a state in which the vehicle is stopped in a parking lot such as a home, and the like.

When a vehicle is used for purposes such as commuting, school, shopping, etc., the time period for which the vehicle is used is often substantially constant. Therefore, the parking period prediction unit 84 predicts the parking period based on, for example, the traveling history information of the vehicle. In this case, the travel history information of the vehicle in the past predetermined period is stored in the memory 62 of the ECU60, for example. The travel history information of the vehicle may be stored in another storage device provided in the vehicle.

The travel history information includes date, day of the week, time period, weather, position of the vehicle, presence or absence of travel of the vehicle, and the like. In addition, when the vehicle is provided with a driver monitoring camera that captures an image generated by a driver of the vehicle, the travel history information may include driver information. In this case, the driver of the vehicle is specified by the driver monitoring camera in order to predict the parking period, and thus the accuracy of the prediction of the parking period can be improved even when the vehicle is used by a plurality of persons.

The parking period prediction unit 84 may predict the parking period based on the current position of the vehicle detected by the GPS receiver 92, the travel route of the vehicle set by the navigation system 94, and the like. The parking period prediction unit 84 may predict the parking period based on information (traffic signal information, traffic congestion information, weather information, and the like) received from the server, the roadside device, or another vehicle by the communication module 95. The parking period prediction unit 84 may predict the parking period by combining the above-described prediction methods.

The parking period prediction unit 84 predicts a parking period in a predetermined period in the future. Fig. 5 is a diagram showing an example of a result of prediction of a parking period. In this example, the parking period prediction unit 84 predicts the parking period of the vehicle in the period of three days in the future (8 months, 9 days to 8 months, 11 days). Fig. 5 shows a traveling period during which the vehicle is predicted to travel and a parking period (hatched portion) during which the vehicle is predicted to stop. The width of the travel period indicates the length of time of the travel period, and the width of the parking period indicates the length of time of the parking period. A parking period number (p is 1-7) is assigned to each of the consecutive parking periods.

The ECU60 also functions as a control device for the internal combustion engine 1. Therefore, the ECU60 controls the internal combustion engine 1 to obtain power for running while the vehicle is running. Therefore, the computational resources of the ECU60 that can be used for learning the neural network model are limited. However, in learning the neural network model, many operations are required to update the weight w and the offset b. Therefore, it is difficult to perform learning with a high computational load during traveling of the vehicle by the ECU 60. In addition, increasing the processing capability of the ECU60 for learning while the vehicle is traveling or increasing the cost of the vehicle by providing an additional ECU for learning.

In the present embodiment, the learning unit 83 learns the neural network model when the vehicle is stopped. This allows the neural network model to be learned when the computational resources of the ECU60 are idle.

However, when the learning time of the neural network model is longer than the parking period, the learning cannot be completed during the parking period. As a result, the neural network model may not be updated at an appropriate frequency, and the accuracy of calculating the output parameters based on the neural network model may deteriorate.

The greater the number of training data sets used for learning, the longer the learning time of the neural network model. Therefore, in order to shorten the learning time, it is necessary to reduce the number of training data sets used in one learning.

The plurality of input parameters of the neural network model each have a predetermined range. The predetermined range is set, for example, as a range between an upper limit value and a lower limit value of values that may occur in the internal combustion engine 1. When learning is performed using a training data set in the entire range of input parameters, a large amount of time is required for learning, and learning cannot be completed during a parking period.

In the present embodiment, the created training data set is divided into a plurality of learning regions, and the training data set in the learning regions is used for each learning region to learn the neural network model. This can reduce the learning time per learning, and can increase the update frequency of the neural network model. Therefore, the neural network model can be efficiently learned in the vehicle.

In order to perform the above-described processing, the data set creating unit 82 divides the training data set into a plurality of learning regions specified based on the ranges of the plurality of input parameters. Fig. 6 is a diagram schematically showing a plurality of learning regions in the first embodiment. In this example, two parameters (input parameter a and input parameter B) are used as input parameters of the neural network model.

The input parameter a has a predetermined range, and the predetermined range is divided into a plurality of regions. Likewise, the input parameter B has a predetermined range, and the predetermined range is divided into a plurality of regions. In this example, the plurality of divided regions have the same width in the input parameter a and the input parameter B.

A space defined by the input parameters a and B (a two-dimensional space in the example of fig. 6) is divided into a plurality of learning regions. Each learning region is defined by a range of input parameters a and a range of input parameters B. Each learning region is assigned a learning region number (i is 1 to n). In addition, the dimensions of the space defined by the plurality of input parameters and the learning region are equal to the number of input parameters. The number of learning regions is a value obtained by multiplying the number of all regions of the plurality of input parameters.

The learning unit 83 learns the neural network model for each learning region. The learning planning unit 81 assigns a plurality of learning regions to the parking period so that the learning of the neural network model is not interrupted during the parking period. In other words, the learning planning unit 81 allocates a plurality of learning regions to the parking period so that the learning of the neural network model in each learning region is completed during the parking period. This makes it possible to complete the learning of the neural network model in each learning region during a continuous parking period, and to increase the update frequency of the neural network model.

In the example of fig. 5, the 1 st parking period (p-1) is assigned the 1 st learning region (i-1), the 2 nd parking period (p-2) is assigned the 2 nd learning region (i-2), the 3 rd parking period (p-3) is assigned the 3 rd learning region (i-3), the 4 th learning region (i-4) and the 5 th learning region (i-5) are assigned to the 4 th parking period (p-4), the 6 th learning region (i-1) to the 12 th learning region (i-12) are assigned to the 5 th parking period (p-5), the 13 th learning region (i-13) and the 14 th learning region (i-14) are assigned to the 6 th parking period (p-6), and the 15 th learning region (i-15) and the 16 th learning region (i-16) are assigned to the 7 th parking period (p-7).

The calculation unit 85 calculates an output parameter using the neural network model. Specifically, the calculation unit 85 inputs the input parameters to the neural network model, and causes the neural network model to output the output parameters. Thus, the output parameter corresponding to the input parameter can be predicted without detecting the actual measurement value of the output parameter by a sensor or the like.

The control unit 86 controls the vehicle based on the value of the output parameter calculated by the calculation unit 85. In the present embodiment, the control unit 86 controls the internal combustion engine 1 based on the value of the output parameter calculated by the calculation unit 85. For example, when the output parameter is the NOx concentration in the exhaust gas, the control unit 86 increases the opening degree of the EGR control valve 15 so that the NOx concentration decreases when the predicted value of the NOx concentration calculated by the calculation unit 85 is higher than the target concentration.

Hereinafter, control for learning a neural network model in a vehicle will be described in detail with reference to flowcharts of fig. 7 to 10.

< processing of data set creation >

Fig. 7 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the data set creation process in the first embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S101, the data set creating unit 82 acquires measured values of input parameters and measured values of output parameters corresponding to the measured values. The actual measurement values of the input parameter and the output parameter are values detected by sensors and the like, and are values calculated based on command values output from the ECU60 to the actuator 91, and the like.

Next, in step S102, the data set creating unit 82 creates a training data set by combining the actual measurement value of the input parameter and the actual measurement value of the output parameter.

Next, in step S103, the data set creating unit 82 sorts the training data set into learning regions. At this time, the training data set is divided into learning regions so that the actual measurement values of the input parameters of the training data set are included in the range of the input parameters defining the learning region. The training data set is stored in the memory 62 of the ECU60 together with the learning region number i of the corresponding learning region. The training data sets stored in the memory 62 are deleted in order from the old data, and the latest predetermined number of training data sets are stored in the memory 62. The training data set may be stored in another storage device provided in the vehicle. After step S103, the present control routine ends.

< prediction processing during parking >

Fig. 8 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the parking period prediction processing in the first embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S201, the parking period prediction unit 84 predicts the parking period using the prediction method described above. Next, in step S202, the parking period predicting unit 84 assigns a parking period number p to the parking period as shown in the example of fig. 5. After step S202, the present control routine ends.

< study plan creation processing >

Fig. 9 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning plan creation process in the first embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S301, the learning planning unit 81 sets the learning region number i and the parking period number p to 1.

Next, in step S302, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not a training data set is present in the i-th learning region. When the memory 62 of the ECU60 stores the training data set classified into the i-th learning region, the learning planning unit 81 determines that the training data set exists in the i-th learning region. If it is determined in step S302 that the training data set is present in the i-th learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S303.

In step S303, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the parking time STp in the p-th parking period is equal to or greater than the learning time L Ti in the i-th learning region, and in this case, the learning planning unit 81 calculates that the learning time L Ti in the i-th learning region is longer as the number of training data sets L Ti. in the i-th learning region is larger, based on the number of training data sets divided into the i-th learning region.

If it is determined in step S303 that the parking time STp in the p-th parking period is equal to or longer than the learning time L Ti in the i-th learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S304. in this case, the learning of the neural network model in the i-th learning region can be completed in the p-th parking period.

Next, in step S305, the learning planning unit 81 updates the parking time STp of the p-th parking period in order to determine whether or not the next learning region can be classified into the p-th parking period, and specifically, the learning planning unit 81 sets a value obtained by subtracting the learning time L Ti of the i-th learning region from the parking time STp of the p-th parking period as a new parking time STp.

After step S305, the present control routine proceeds to step S308. If it is determined in step S302 that the training data set does not exist in the i-th learning region, the control routine proceeds to step S308. In step S308, the learning planning unit 81 adds 1 to the learning region number i. Next, in step S309, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the learning region number i is n + 1. As shown in fig. 6, n is the total number of predetermined learning regions.

If it is determined in step S309 that the learning region number i is n +1, the present control routine is ended. The training data set and the prediction result of the parking period in each learning region are repeatedly updated by the control routine of fig. 7 and 8. Therefore, in the next control routine, the allocation of the learning region is restarted from the beginning.

On the other hand, if it is determined in step S309 that the learning region number i is equal to or less than n, the control routine proceeds to step S310. In step S310, the learning planning unit 81 sets the parking period number p to 1. After step S310, the control routine returns to step S302 to determine whether the next learning region can be allocated.

If it is determined in step S303 that the parking time STp in the p-th parking period is smaller than the learning time L Ti in the i-th learning region, the control routine proceeds to step S306, and in step S306, the learning planning unit 81 adds 1 to the parking period number in order to search for another parking period to which the i-th learning region can be assigned.

Next, in step S307, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the parking period number p is m + 1. m is the total number of predicted parking periods, which is 7 in the example of fig. 5. If it is determined in step S307 that the parking period number p is m or less, the control routine returns to step S303 to determine whether or not allocation to the next parking period is possible.

On the other hand, if it is determined in step S307 that parking period number p is m +1, since there is no parking period to which the i-th learning region can be assigned, 1 is added to learning region number i in step S308.

Next, in step S309, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the learning region number i is n + 1. When it is determined that the learning region number i is n +1, the present control routine is ended. On the other hand, when it is determined that the learning region number i is equal to or less than n, the control routine proceeds to step S310, and the subsequent processing is the processing described above.

As described above, in the present control routine, whether or not allocation is possible is determined in order from the learning region having the small learning region number i. As a result, the learning region having the relatively small learning region number i is preferentially allocated to the parking period over the learning region having the relatively large learning region number i. That is, in the present embodiment, the learning region number i indicates the priority order of learning, and the smaller the learning region number i, the higher the priority order of learning in the learning region. Therefore, it can be said that the plurality of learning regions are given priority to learning. In the example of fig. 6, the order of priority is given in the order of the arrangement of the learning regions, but the order of priority may be given randomly, for example.

< learning processing >

Fig. 10 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning process in the first embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU 60.

First, in step S401, the learning unit 83 determines whether or not the vehicle is currently stopped. For example, when the state in which the speed of the vehicle detected by the vehicle speed sensor 77 is zero continues for a predetermined time or more, the learning unit 83 determines that the vehicle is currently in the parking period. If it is determined in step S401 that the vehicle is not currently parked, that is, if it is determined that the vehicle is currently traveling, the control routine is terminated.

On the other hand, if it is determined in step S401 that the vehicle is currently parked, the control routine proceeds to step S402. In step S402, the learning unit 83 compares the date and time of the parking period predicted by the parking period prediction unit 84 with the current date and time, and thereby determines the parking period number p of the current parking period.

Next, in step S402, the learning unit 83 determines whether or not a learning region is assigned to the parking period of the parking period number p specified in step S402. When it is determined that the learning region is not allocated, the present control routine is ended. On the other hand, when it is determined that the learning region is allocated, the control routine proceeds to step S404.

In step S404, the learning unit 83 learns the neural network model in the assigned learning region. Specifically, the learning unit 83 repeatedly updates the values of the weight w and the bias b in the neural network model by the above-described error back propagation method using the training data set in the assigned learning region. After step S404, the present control routine ends.

The learning unit 83 updates the neural network model after learning is completed. Specifically, the learning unit 83 changes the values of the weight w and the offset b in the neural network model to the final values updated by the learning. The calculation unit 85 calculates an output parameter using the updated neural network model.

< second embodiment >

The machine learning device according to the second embodiment is basically the same as the machine learning device according to the first embodiment in configuration and control except for the points described below. Therefore, the second embodiment of the present invention will be described below mainly focusing on the differences from the first embodiment.

In the first embodiment, the plurality of learning regions are each defined by a combination in which the ranges of the input parameters are different. On the other hand, in the second embodiment, the plurality of learning regions includes an elementary school learning region and a college learning region including the elementary school learning region. The small learning region and the university learning region are determined such that the data density of the small learning region is higher than that of the university learning region. That is, the elementary school learning area is defined by a range of input parameters having a relatively high frequency of appearance, and the difference area between the university learning area and the elementary school learning area is defined by a range of input parameters having a relatively low frequency of appearance.

The learning section 83 selectively assigns the elementary school learning region and the university learning region to the parking period. In this case, the training data set in the elementary school learning area is always used in the learning of the neural network model. Therefore, learning of the neural network model can be promoted with respect to the range of the input parameter having a relatively high frequency of occurrence. As a result, the accuracy of calculating the output parameter by the neural network model in the typical traveling state of the vehicle can be improved.

Fig. 11 is a diagram schematically showing a plurality of learning regions in the second embodiment. In this example, the 2 nd learning region (i ═ 2) includes the 1 st learning region (i ═ 1), and the 3 rd learning region (i ═ 3) includes the 1 st learning region (i ═ 1) and the 2 nd learning region (i ═ 2). Therefore, the 1 st learning region corresponds to the elementary school learning region, and the 2 nd learning region and the 3 rd learning region correspond to the college learning region. The number of university study areas may be other than 2.

For example, the elementary school learning region and the university learning region are predetermined such that the data density of the small learning region is higher than the data density of the university learning region based on the prediction of the frequency of appearance of the range of each of the plurality of input parameters. In the second embodiment, the control routine of fig. 12 is executed in place of the control routine of fig. 9 in addition to the control routines of fig. 7, 8, and 10. Fig. 12 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning plan creation process in the second embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S501, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not a training data set is present in the i-th learning region, as in step S301 of fig. 9. The initial value of the learning region number i is 1. If it is determined that the training data set does not exist in the i-th learning region, the control routine is terminated. On the other hand, if it is determined that the training data set exists in the i-th learning region, the control routine proceeds to step S502. In step S502, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the parking time STp in the p-th parking period is equal to or greater than the learning time L T3 in the 3 rd learning region, and in this case, the learning planning unit 81 calculates the learning time L T3 in the 3 rd learning region based on the number of training data sets classified into the 3 rd learning region, and the learning time L T3 in the 3 rd learning region is longer as the number of training data sets is larger.

If it is determined in step S502 that the parking time STp in the p-th parking period is equal to or longer than the learning time L T3 in the 3 rd learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S503. in step S503, the learning planning unit 81 assigns the 3 rd learning region to the p-th parking period.

Next, in step S508, the learning planning unit 81 adds 1 to the parking period number p in order to determine whether or not to assign the next parking period. Next, in step S509, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the parking period number p is m + 1. m is the total number of predicted parking periods.

If it is determined in step S509 that the parking period number p is m or less, the present control routine is ended. On the other hand, if it is determined in step S509 that the parking period number p is m +1, the control routine proceeds to step S510. If it is determined in step S504 that the parking time STp in the p-th parking period is equal to or longer than the learning time L T2 in the 2 nd learning region, the control routine proceeds to step S505, and in step S505, the learning planning unit 81 assigns the 2 nd learning region to the p-th parking period, and then, steps S508 to S510 are executed as described above.

On the other hand, when it is determined in step S504 that the parking time STp in the p-th parking period is smaller than the learning time L T2 in the 2-th learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S506. in step S506, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the parking time STp in the p-th parking period is equal to or greater than the learning time L T1 in the 1-th learning region. in this case, the learning planning unit 81 calculates the learning time L T1 in the 1-th learning region based on the number of training data sets divided into the 1-th learning region, and the learning time L T1 in the 1-th learning region is longer as the number of training data sets is larger, and further, since the 3-th learning region and the 2-th learning region include the 1-th learning region, the learning time L T1 in the 1-th learning region is equal to or shorter than the learning time L T3 in the 3-th learning region and the learning time L T2 in the 2-.

If it is determined in step S506 that the parking time STp in the p-th parking period is equal to or longer than the learning time L T1 in the 1 st learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S507, and in step S507, the learning planning unit 81 assigns the 1 st learning region to the p-th parking period, and then, steps S508 to S510 are executed as described above.

On the other hand, if it is determined in step S506 that the parking time STp in the p-th parking period is smaller than the learning time L T1 in the 1 st learning region, the present control routine proceeds to step S508, and steps S508 to S510 are executed as described above.

< third embodiment >

The machine learning device according to the third embodiment is basically the same as the machine learning device according to the first embodiment in configuration and control except for the points described below. Therefore, the following description will focus on a third embodiment of the present invention, which is different from the first embodiment.

In the third embodiment, the plurality of learning regions are given learning priorities as in the first embodiment. On the other hand, in the third embodiment, unlike the first embodiment, the learning planning unit 81 increases the priority of learning in a learning region including a value of an input parameter having a relatively high frequency of occurrence to a higher priority of learning in a learning region including a value of an input parameter having a relatively low frequency of occurrence. Therefore, learning of the neural network model can be promoted with respect to the range of the input parameter having a relatively high frequency of occurrence. As a result, the accuracy of calculating the output parameter by the neural network model in the typical traveling state of the vehicle can be improved.

In the third embodiment, a space defined by a plurality of input parameters is divided into a plurality of initial regions. The plurality of initial regions are divided into three learning regions (a 1 st learning region, a 2 nd learning region, and a 3 rd learning region) based on the number of times of acquisition of actual measurement values of input parameters acquired in the vehicle. The initial region is the same region as the learning region shown in fig. 5. In the third embodiment, the number of learning regions may be any number of two or more.

In the third embodiment, the control routine of fig. 7 to 10 is executed as in the first embodiment. In this case, in the third embodiment, in step S103 of fig. 7, the data set creating unit 82 classifies the training data set into the learning region and the initial region. In this case, the training data set is stored in the memory 62 of the ECU60 together with the learning region number i of the corresponding learning region and the initial region number q of the corresponding initial region.

< learning region setting processing >

In the third embodiment, the control routine of fig. 13 is executed in addition to the control routines of fig. 7 to 10. Fig. 13 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning region setting process in the third embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S601, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the number Nq of training data sets classified into the qth initial region is equal to or greater than the 1 st reference value R1. The 1 st reference value R1 is predetermined. The initial value of the initial region number q is 1.

If it is determined in step S601 that the number Nq of training data sets is equal to or greater than the 1 st reference value R1, the present control routine proceeds to step S602. In step S602, the learning planning unit 81 sets the learning region number i of the qth initial region to 1.

Next, in step S607, the learning planning unit 81 adds 1 to the initial region number q in order to set the learning region number i of the next initial region. Next, in step S608, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the initial region number q is k + 1. k is the total number of predetermined initial regions.

If it is determined in step S608 that the initial region number q is k or less, the present control routine is ended. On the other hand, if it is determined in step S608 that the initial region number q is k +1, the present control routine proceeds to step S609. In step S609, the learning planning unit 81 resets the initial region number q to 1 (initial value). After step S609, the present control routine ends.

On the other hand, if it is determined in step S601 that the number Nq of training data sets is smaller than the 1 st reference value R1, the present control routine proceeds to step S603. In step S603, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the number Nq of training data sets classified into the qth initial region is equal to or greater than a 2 nd reference value R2. The 2 nd reference value R2 is predetermined and set to a value smaller than the 1 st reference value R1.

If it is determined in step S603 that the number Nq of training data sets is equal to or greater than the 2 nd reference value R2, the present control routine proceeds to step S604. In step S604, the learning planning unit 81 sets the learning region number i of the qth initial region to 2. In the control routine of fig. 9, the 1 st learning region is assigned to the parking period with priority over the 2 nd learning region. Therefore, the order of priority of learning in the 2 nd learning region is lower than that in the 1 st learning region. Next, step S607 to step S609 are executed as described above.

On the other hand, if it is determined in step S603 that the number Nq of training data sets is smaller than the 2 nd reference value R2, the present control routine proceeds to step S605. In step S605, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the number Nq of training data sets classified into the qth initial region is equal to or greater than a 3 rd reference value R3. The 3 rd reference value R3 is predetermined and set to a value smaller than the 1 st reference value R1 and the 2 nd reference value R2.

If it is determined in step S605 that the number Nq of training data sets is equal to or greater than the 3 rd reference value R3, the present control routine proceeds to step S606. In step S606, the learning planning unit 81 sets the learning region number i of the qth initial region to 3. In the control routine of fig. 9, the 1 st learning region and the 2 nd learning region are assigned to the parking period with priority over the 3 rd learning region. Therefore, the priority order of learning in the 3 rd learning region is lower than the priority order of learning in the 1 st learning region and the 2 nd learning region. Next, step S607 to step S609 are executed as described above.

< fourth embodiment >

The machine learning device according to the fourth embodiment is basically the same as the machine learning device according to the first embodiment in configuration and control except for the points described below. Therefore, the following description will focus on a fourth embodiment of the present invention, which is different from the first embodiment.

In the fourth embodiment, the learning unit 83 learns a plurality of neural network models. The plurality of neural network models output different types of output parameters, respectively.

For example, the learning unit 83 learns six neural network models. For example,in the 1 st neural network model, the input parameters include an engine speed, a fresh air amount, and an ignition timing, and the output parameters include a Hydrocarbon (HC) concentration in exhaust gas. In addition, in the 2 nd neural network model, the input parameters include the engine speed, the fresh air amount, and the EGR gas amount, and the output parameters include the NOx concentration in the exhaust gas. In addition, in the 3 rd neural network model, the input parameters include an engine speed, a fresh air amount, an EGR amount, and an ignition timing, and the output parameters include a carbon monoxide (CO) concentration in the exhaust gas. In addition, in the 4 th neural network model, the input parameters include the engine speed, the fresh air amount, and the fuel injection amount, and the output parameters include the fuel economy of the vehicle. In addition, in the 5 th neural network model, the input parameters include the engine speed, the fresh air amount, and the ignition timing, and the output parameters include the output torque of the internal combustion engine 1. In addition, in the 6 th neural network model, the input parameters include the engine speed, the fresh air amount, and the fuel injection amount, and the output parameters include carbon dioxide (CO) in the exhaust gas2) And (4) concentration.

In this case, the actual measurement values of the input parameter and the output parameter can be obtained as follows. The engine speed is calculated based on the output of the crank angle sensor 74. The fresh air amount is detected by the air flow meter 71. The ignition timing is calculated based on a command value from the ECU60 to the spark plug. The EGR gas amount is calculated based on the opening degree of the EGR control valve 15 and the like. The fuel injection amount is calculated based on a command value from the ECU60 to the fuel injection valve. The NOx concentration in the exhaust gas is detected by the NOx sensor 73. The fuel economy of the vehicle is calculated by, for example, dividing the travel distance by the fuel usage amount. The HC concentration, CO concentration, and CO2 concentration in the exhaust gas are calculated based on the output of the air-fuel ratio sensor 72, for example. These concentrations may be directly detected by an exhaust gas sensor that detects the concentration of a predetermined component.

In the fourth embodiment, a space defined by a plurality of input parameters is divided into a plurality of learning regions for each of a plurality of neural network models. Different learning regions of the neural network model are assigned with different learning region numbers. In addition, as in the first embodiment, the plurality of learning regions are given learning priority orders.

When a plurality of neural network models that output different output parameters are learned, the priority of the learning of the neural network models changes depending on information on the road on which the vehicle is traveling, and the like. Therefore, the learning planning unit 81 changes the learning priority order given to the plurality of learning regions based on the information on the road on which the vehicle travels. This makes it possible to adapt the neural network model to the driving state of the vehicle.

For example, when the road on which the vehicle is traveling is an uphill slope, the internal combustion engine 1 needs to generate power required for the uphill slope. Therefore, in order to improve the accuracy of calculating the output torque of the internal combustion engine 1, the learning priority order of the neural network model (5 th neural network model) that outputs the output torque of the internal combustion engine 1 is highest.

Therefore, when the road on which the vehicle is traveling is an uphill slope, the learning planning unit 81 increases the priority order of the learning region corresponding to the 5 th neural network model, as compared to when the road on which the vehicle is traveling is not an uphill slope.

< learning area number Change processing >

In the fourth embodiment, the control routine of fig. 14 is executed in addition to the control routines of fig. 7 to 10. Fig. 14 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning region number changing process in the fourth embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S801, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the road on which the vehicle is traveling is an uphill. For example, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the road on which the vehicle is traveling is an uphill based on the current position of the vehicle detected by the GPS receiver 92 and the map information stored in the map database 93.

If it is determined in step S801 that the road on which the vehicle is traveling is not an uphill, the present control routine proceeds to step S803. In step S803, the learning planning unit 81 initializes the learning region number i. That is, the learning region numbers i of all the learning regions are set to predetermined initial values. After step S803, the present control routine ends.

On the other hand, if it is determined in step S801 that the road is an uphill, the present control routine proceeds to step S802. In step S802, the learning planning unit 81 changes the learning region number i from the initial value. Specifically, the learning planning unit 81 reduces the learning region number i of the learning region corresponding to the 5 th neural network model that outputs the output torque of the internal combustion engine 1. For example, the learning region number i of the corresponding learning region is reduced in the order of the 6 th, 4 th, 3 rd, 1 st, 2 nd, and 5 th neural network models. After step S802, the present control routine ends.

Further, when the vehicle travels on an expressway, the frequency of occurrence of the speed of the vehicle in a predetermined range (for example, 80km/h to 120km/h) becomes high. Therefore, the learning planning unit 81 may increase the priority ranking of the learning region including the vehicle speed in the predetermined range, when the road on which the vehicle travels is an expressway, as compared with a case where the road on which the vehicle travels is not an expressway. In this case, the learning unit 83 learns a neural network model including the speed of the vehicle as an input parameter. In this case, the learning unit 83 may perform learning of only one neural network model.

< fifth embodiment >

The configuration and control of the machine learning device according to the fifth embodiment are basically the same as those of the machine learning device according to the fourth embodiment except for the points described below. Therefore, the following description will focus on a portion different from the fourth embodiment regarding the fifth embodiment of the present invention.

When the target of the neural network model is the internal combustion engine 1 and a plurality of neural network models that output different output parameters are learned as in the fourth embodiment, the priority order of learning of the neural network models changes depending on the warm-up state of the internal combustion engine 1. Therefore, the learning planning unit 81 changes the priority order of learning to be given to the plurality of learning regions based on the warm-up state of the internal combustion engine 1. This makes it possible to adapt the neural network model to the state of the internal combustion engine 1.

In the case where the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is not completed, the purification performance of the catalyst 29 is low. Therefore, in order to suppress deterioration of exhaust emission, it is necessary to improve the calculation accuracy of the harmful substance concentrations (NOx, HC, and CO) in the exhaust gas. On the other hand, when the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is completed, the fuel economy of the vehicle is prioritized. Therefore, when the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is not completed, the learning planning unit 81 increases the priority order of the learning region corresponding to the neural network model (1 st to 3 rd neural network models) that outputs the concentration of the harmful substance in the exhaust gas, and decreases the priority order of the learning region corresponding to the neural network model (4 th neural network model) that outputs the fuel economy of the vehicle, as compared to the case where the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is completed.

< learning area number Change processing >

In the fifth embodiment, the control routine of fig. 15 is executed in addition to the control routines of fig. 7 to 10. Fig. 15 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the learning region number changing process in the fifth embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU60 at predetermined time intervals.

First, in step S901, the learning planning unit 81 acquires the warm-up state of the internal combustion engine 1. Specifically, the learning planning unit 81 determines whether or not the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is completed. This determination is performed based on, for example, the output of a water temperature sensor provided in the internal combustion engine 1, the output of an exhaust gas temperature sensor provided in the exhaust passage of the internal combustion engine 1, the integrated fresh air amount calculated from the output of the air flow meter 71, and the like.

Next, in step S902, the learning planning unit 81 changes the learning region number i. Specifically, when the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is not completed, the learning planning unit 81 decreases the learning region numbers i of the learning regions corresponding to the 1 st to 3 rd neural network models that output the harmful substance concentration in the exhaust gas and increases the learning region number i of the learning region corresponding to the 4 th neural network model that outputs the fuel economy of the vehicle, as compared to the case where the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is completed.

For example, when the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is not completed, the learning region number i of the corresponding learning region is decreased in the order of the 6 th neural network model, the 5 th neural network model, the 4 th neural network model, the 3 rd neural network model, the 2 nd neural network model, and the 1 st neural network model. On the other hand, when the warm-up of the internal combustion engine 1 is completed, the learning region number i of the corresponding learning region is decreased in the order of the 6 th, 5 th, 3 rd, 1 st, 2 nd, and 4 th neural network models. After step S902, the present control routine ends.

< other embodiments >

While the preferred embodiments of the present invention have been described above, the present invention is not limited to these embodiments, and various modifications and changes can be made within the scope of the claims.

For example, the object of the neural network model may be other than the internal combustion engine 1 as long as it is related to the vehicle. For example, the object of the neural network model may be the vehicle itself, a compression self-ignition internal combustion engine (diesel engine), a transmission, or the like.

The vehicle on which the machine learning device is mounted may be a Hybrid Vehicle (HV), a plug-in hybrid vehicle (PHV), or an Electric Vehicle (EV) that includes an electric motor as a drive source. In this case, the target of the neural network model may be a motor, a battery that supplies electric power to the motor, or the like.

In addition, as the input parameters and the output parameters of the neural network model, various parameters can be used according to the object of the neural network model. The sensor for detecting the actual measurement value of the input parameter or the output parameter is selected according to the kind of the input parameter and the output parameter.

The above embodiments may be implemented in any combination. For example, the fourth embodiment may be combined with the fifth embodiment. In this case, for example, in the control routine of fig. 14, step S901 and step S902 of fig. 15 are executed instead of step S803.
